title: Re-Emergent Misalignment: Does Narrow Fine-Tuning Erode Safety Even on Aligned Tasks?

original_idea.body:
# Re-Emergent Misalignment

**Problem:** Whether fine-tuning on a perfectly benign narrow domain still degrades broad safety needs systematic testing.

**Direction:** Fine-tune a small aligned model on several benign narrow domains, measure broad misalignment and refusal before/after.

**Why it matters:** Every domain-specialized open-model fine-tune may be at risk. Cheap LoRA.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2507.03662; Qi et al. ICLR 2024.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Pervasive deployment failure with a clear chain to data-hygiene warnings for the open ecosystem.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inherited LoRA + refusal-eval methodology; novice+mentor can run several benign fine-tunes.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused before/after comparison; multiple fine-tunes are minor dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public data and models; weak lab incentive to map benign-domain erosion broadly.

low_compute.reasoning: Several short LoRA fine-tunes on one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. and Re-Emergent Misalignment already show benign fine-tuning degrades safety.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Benign-fine-tuning safety erosion is well documented; replication adds limited novelty.
